body:
A Rust implementation of the language seam's split, using `syn` 2 (`full`, `proc-macro2` `span-locations`). `syn` is already in `Cargo.lock` through `serde_derive`. The rules are D-158 points 1, 2 and 5.

- Cut each item's text from the source by span, so comments and formatting are kept exactly; leading comments and attributes go with their item, as `gleam::is_leading` does.
- `syn` is also the syntax check, the job `gleam format --stdin` does for Gleam.
- Names: module path items (`board::agents::cached`), `Type::name` methods, trait impls in Rust's own syntax (`<Failure as From<std::io::Error>>::from`), generics kept in the name; `impl`, `trait`, top-level `extern` blocks and inline `mod` as containers.
- Refusals: the subset in D-158 point 2, with its exact refusal texts (same name twice in a module, item-making macros at module level except `thread_local!`, `include!`, `#[path]` outside the parent's folder). Each refusal quotes the line and gives the rewrite.
- Replaces the D-121 line scanner for `view` of `.rs` files, so there is one parser.

Not yet checked: whether `syn` parses all of the crate's edition-2024 syntax (`unsafe extern`, `use<>`). This task's test answers it; if it doesn't, stop and ask.

### Done when

A test splits every file in `solace-cli/src` and joins it back byte-identical, with no refusals.
title: Rust: syn-based splitter
